chunks: And from him, from Ali, from his father, from Hammad, from Ribi'i, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
"Take the pebbles of the Jamarat from Jummah (Al-Muzdalifah); and if you take them from your saddlebag in Mina, it will suffice you."
And it is permissible to take the pebbles from the rest of the Haram (sanctuary), excluding the Sacred Mosque and the Mosque of Al-Khaif. This was narrated.
ai.seo_question: Where can a pilgrim collect the pebbles for stoning the Jamarat during Hajj?
ai.summary: This narration from Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies the flexibility in sourcing the seven pebbles for Ramy al-Jamarat, affirming that while collecting them from Muzdalifah is standard, retrieving them from one's saddle in Mina is equally valid. It further delineates the geographical boundaries of the Haram, permitting collection from the broader sacred precincts but excluding the specific sanctity of Masjid al-Haram and Masjid al-Khaif, reflecting the juristic precision of Shia fiqh regarding ritual purity and location.
